speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me exactly which antibiotic you were taking and when the rash and joint pain started in relation to your last dose? Also, has the rash spread to your palms and soles?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old girl. The patient was brought to the emergency department because of a 2-day history of low-grade fever, itchy rash, and generalized joint pain. The rash initially started in the antecubital and popliteal fossae before spreading to the trunk and distal extremities. One week ago, she was diagnosed with acute sinusitis and started on amoxicillin. She has no history of adverse drug reactions, and her immunizations are up to date.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any swelling in your hands or feet, or any pain in your lower back? REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis: Appearance Normal, WBC Within normal limits, RBC Within normal limits, Protein Negative, Glucose Negative

speaker: Doctor
text: Has she experienced any abdominal pain or noticed dark, bloody stools? Are her joints visibly swollen or tender to the touch?

speaker: Doctor
text: Are the rash lesions palpable or raised, and have you observed any swelling or tenderness in her joints? REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the CBC is unavailable, let's focus on the clinical signs: are the rash lesions palpable (raised) and non-blanching, and is there significant swelling or tenderness in her joints? Has she had any recent upper respiratory infection prior to the sinusitis?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Diagnosed with acute sinusitis one week ago, no known history of adverse drug reactions, immunizations up to date. Social history: No significant social history provided.

speaker: Doctor
text: The rash description of starting in the antecubital and popliteal fossae is classic for Henoch-Schönlein Purpura, but I need to confirm the nature of the lesions. Are the spots palpable and non-blanching (purpuric), or are they flat and red (maculopapular)?

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the classic distribution of the rash in the flexural areas and the presence of joint pain, I am suspecting Henoch-Schönlein Purpura despite the normal urinalysis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Henoch-Schönlein Purpura (IgA Vasculitis)
